Signing Infrastructure2-of-N threshold, transparency log, reproducible builds.

Cyber Resilience Act Annex I requires signed updates, an integrity mechanism, and a public vulnerability-handling process. Annex II adds SBOM per release + coordinated disclosure + 24-hour reporting. We design and deploy the infrastructure to satisfy all of it as a working reference implementation on your infrastructure: 2-of-N threshold signing across separated jurisdictions, RFC 6962 Merkle-tree transparency log, SBOM automation per release in SPDX + CycloneDX, and third-party reproducibility CI mirrors.

WHY IT EXISTS

Signed updates + SBOM
are where most CRA remediation plans stall.

A gap analysis is easy. Most product teams stall on building the infrastructure to close the gap: signed updates with 2-of-N threshold approval, a public Merkle-tree transparency log, SBOM automation per release, reproducibility CI mirrors that third parties can verify. The primitives are well-known; the integration is 2-4 months of specialist work. We compress it into 4-6 weeks + hand you a working reference implementation.

F·01

Single-key signing is one operator away from disaster

Most product teams sign releases with a single key held by one operator. One compromised laptop, one bribed employee, one accidental commit of the private key, and your entire user base is vulnerable to a malicious release pushed under your identity.

F·02

SBOMs generated as an afterthought

Running `pip freeze > requirements.txt` and calling it an SBOM does not meet CRA Annex I. Regulators + downstream buyers expect signed SPDX + CycloneDX per release with vulnerability-scanning integration. Getting there is an infrastructure project.

F·03

No transparency log means "trust us"

Without a public append-only log of your signed releases, users have no way to verify that the binary they received matches what you signed + published. RFC 6962-style Merkle transparency logs are well-understood but require deployment discipline most product teams haven't invested in.

F·04

Non-reproducible builds mean the SBOM is a fiction

If your build is not reproducible, the SBOM you publish reflects hopes rather than reality: an attacker who compromised your build pipeline could ship anything and the SBOM would still "match." Reproducibility CI mirrors on separated infrastructure catch this. Most teams have not set one up.

WHO IT SERVES

Firms shipping software or firmware
to EU customers under CRA scope.

CRA "product with digital elements" manufacturers

Any firm placing a networked product on the EU market after September 11 2026. Signed updates + SBOM + coordinated disclosure are Annex I + Annex II obligations. This service builds the mechanism.

Software vendors shipping updates to installed base

Desktop applications, browser extensions, mobile apps with sideloadable variants, self-hosted server software, IoT firmware. If "install this update" is a trust-critical operation for your users, threshold signing + transparency log + SBOM discipline are the right posture.

Firms with public trust as a differentiator

Products that market "verifiable" / "no telemetry" / "no cloud dependency". The trust claims mean less without infrastructure users can verify. Transparency log + reproducibility CI mirrors turn marketing claims into verifiable facts.

Firms rebuilding after a supply-chain incident

Post-SolarWinds, post-XZ Utils, post-any-signing-compromise incident, boards ask "why can't this happen to us?" The right answer is 2-of-N threshold signing + transparency log + reproducibility mirrors. This engagement builds it.

Open-source SaaS + hybrid deployment firms

Firms that ship both a cloud service + a self-hostable variant need strong supply-chain guarantees: customers rebuilding + running the self-hostable version must be able to verify the binary matches source.

Design + working reference,
deployed on your infrastructure.

01

Full architecture design document

25-40-page architecture doc covering threshold-signing scheme (2-of-N Ed25519 across specified jurisdictions), transparency-log deployment (RFC 6962 Merkle tree), SBOM automation pipeline (SPDX + CycloneDX per release), reproducibility CI mirror design (2-3 independent build environments). We review it with your engineering + security leads.

02

2-of-N threshold signing setup

Operator identity provisioning (Yubikey 5 NFC per operator, offline signing procedures), key ceremony documentation, cross-jurisdiction operator recommendations, signing-workflow SOPs, key-rotation runbook. We conduct or facilitate the key generation ceremony, depending on your preference.

03

Transparency-log deployment

RFC 6962-style Merkle-tree transparency log deployed on your infrastructure (Postgres + Cloudflare Worker mirror or equivalent). Signed root publication, inclusion-proof endpoints, public read APIs, monitoring + alerting. Delivered as running code.

04

SBOM automation per release

CI pipeline integration: SPDX + CycloneDX SBOM generated per build, signed by 2-of-N operators, published to SBOM endpoint, linked from Declaration of Conformity. Dependency-scanning integration (Trivy / Grype / equivalent) with defined vulnerability-triage workflow.

05

Reproducibility CI mirrors

2-3 independent CI environments (recommend Berlin + Reykjavik + your primary) continuously building your source + comparing hash to your primary build's output. Divergence alerts + public reproducibility manifests. This is the mechanism that catches supply-chain compromise before users are affected.

06

Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure policy + bug bounty setup

Public CVD policy at `yourdomain/security` covering Annex II obligations (24-hour actively-exploited-vuln reporting, patch SLAs per CVSS severity, coordinated disclosure timeline). Bug-bounty programme scoping (VF Empire uses €500-€25 000 tiered; we recommend appropriate scale for your product).

07

Ongoing operational runbooks

Key rotation runbook, firmware/software release runbook (with 15-minute inspection window), incident response runbook covering signing-key compromise, transparency-log split-view detection, reproducibility-mismatch response, emergency signing procedures. All documented in the style of VF Empire's own public runbooks.

08

Weekly working sessions + knowledge transfer

Weekly 90-minute working sessions with your team throughout the engagement. Concludes with a full knowledge-transfer session so your team owns and operates the infrastructure post-delivery without VF Empire.

WEEK 0

Kick-off with your engineering + security + release-management leads. We map your current release process and inventory existing CI + signing + SBOM state. Threat model input (Service 02 output or your own). We sign an NDA if needed.

Architecture design + operator selection

We design the full architecture and discuss operator identity + jurisdiction recommendations with you. Hardware procurement starts (Yubikey 5 NFC, ~€60 each). Cross-jurisdiction operator engagements start (if using an external contractor as second operator).

WEEK 2

Key-generation ceremonies with each operator (physical, offline, witnessed). We write operator SOPs, prototype the signing workflow, and sign test releases end-to-end.

WEEK 3

We deploy the transparency log, get signed root publication working, and integrate SBOM generation into CI. We sign, log and publish the SBOM for a first test release end-to-end.

WEEK 4

Reproducibility CI mirrors + hardening

We deploy 2-3 independent build environments, complete the first reproducibility check, and configure divergence alerting. Standard tier engagement complete. Extended tier continues.

WEEK 5-6

Runbooks + knowledge transfer (Extended tier)

We write the full ops runbooks and review them with your team, practise emergency-signing procedures, and run the first quarterly key-rotation drill. Post-engagement 8-week Q&A window begins.

COMMON QUESTIONS

What most first calls ask.

Can't we use Sigstore / cosign / a hosted service instead?

Sigstore is an excellent tool; we use it as a component in many deployments. The question is what trust root you sign against + how threshold approval works + who operates the transparency log. Sigstore's public infrastructure is US-hosted; for EU CRA compliance many firms prefer their own transparency log on EU infrastructure. We can layer Sigstore into your architecture or replace it with an EU-sovereign stack. Your choice, informed by your regulatory posture.

Do we need a second operator in a different jurisdiction?

CRA does not require it. We recommend it if your product ships to a broad user base. A single operator = single point of failure (compromise / coercion / accident). VF Empire uses 2-of-2 across MT + DE for exactly this reason. If you can't find a second operator, VF Empire can serve on retainer (~€1500/mo, separate engagement) once we understand your product.

How much does the ongoing infrastructure cost to operate?

At typical release cadence (monthly minor + quarterly major): Yubikey hardware €120 one-off (2 keys), Hetzner + Cloudflare €200-500/mo for transparency-log + SBOM + reproducibility-mirror infrastructure, retained second operator €1500/mo optional. Total operational cost ≈ €2 000-3 000/mo at scale. Much less at lower cadence.

Our CI is on GitHub Actions / GitLab / self-hosted. Will it work?

Yes to all. Reproducibility CI mirrors are separate from your primary CI (that's the point): they run on their own infrastructure and compare output to your primary. Any modern CI platform integrates with SBOM generation + signing. We adapt to your stack.

What if we can't source a second signing operator?

You have three options: (1) use 2-of-2 with two of your own trusted operators in different physical locations (weaker than cross-jurisdiction but better than single-key), (2) VF Empire serves as second operator on retainer (independent + jurisdictionally-separate), (3) engage a third-party signing service (Chainguard, Sigstore-hosted, others). We recommend based on your product's risk profile.

How is this different from what SLSA / SSDF / NIST 800-218 recommend?

Aligned. SLSA / SSDF / NIST 800-218 describe *what* to do at the framework level; this engagement is the *implementation*: the deployment of threshold signing + transparency log + SBOM automation + reproducibility that satisfies those frameworks + CRA obligations.

NDA + payment terms?

Standard mutual NDA within 24 hours of request. Invoice in EUR by VF Empire Corp Ltd (Malta) or Noirda GmbH (Germany). Payment terms: 40% kick-off / 30% mid-engagement / 30% delivery. SEPA transfer.
